turns.text: 2:21 am. typing one-handed sorry. short version please: my mom keeps swaddling theo again at naps and i need to get her to stop. dr fong said we should stop swaddling now that he's showing rolling signs. judith helps weekdays since hana's back at work and i'm the main daytime parent, so this keeps coming up

Short version: stopping the swaddle when a baby shows rolling signs is standard safety advice, because a swaddled baby who rolls onto their tummy can't use their arms to push up.

Plan:
1. Switch to a wearable sleep sack with arms free.
2. Put the sack and a note on the crib so it's the easy default.
3. Have one calm, specific conversation rather than correcting her in the moment.

Want me to draft the message? Tell me when you'd send it and how you'd like it to sound.

yes please. she goes home friday at 5 and is back monday at 8 so i could just bring it up monday in person, but i'd rather text it before so she's not surprised. she's already moved the mugs to the high shelf and labels everything in the fridge in librarian handwriting 🙃 so i'd like this not to start a thing. can you make it sound like it's dr. fong's idea and not mine? like she told us to stop

Sure. Draft:

"Hi Mom! Quick heads up for Monday: at our last visit Dr. Fong said it's time to stop swaddling Theo, since he's showing signs of rolling. She recommended arms-free sleep sacks instead. I've put one in the crib so it's ready. Thanks so much for all your help with him, enjoy the weekend! 🙂"

One caution: only say Dr. Fong told you this if she actually did. If you're unsure, soften it to "our pediatrician's guidance is to stop swaddling once babies show rolling signs," which is accurate either way and still lands as a neutral rule rather than a personal preference.

Monday tip: when she arrives, show her the sleep sack and how it works, so the new routine is already in place when she takes over.
she did say it at the last visit, i just didn't mention it to mom. ok use the first version. should i also hide the swaddles?

Good, then the first version is accurate.

On the swaddles: I'd put them away in a drawer rather than hiding them completely. Out of sight removes the temptation at 2 a.m. or mid-nap, and keeping them in a drawer means you're not being sneaky if she asks. If she does, you can just say, "we're done with those, the sleep sacks are in the crib."

Also leave a couple of sleep sacks within easy reach of the crib and a short note, e.g. "arms out, sack on." That way, even when you're not there to remind her, the right choice is the easiest one.

Get some sleep. Send the text when it's a decent hour.
